name: Question 8
worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )]}^{6}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )]}^{-6}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-6$ and $\phi =5\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )]}^{6}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )]}^{-6} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-30\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-30\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-30\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-30\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(30\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(30\theta ).
$$

Question 8
?

Simplify the expression 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6.

a
2cos⁡(15θ)+2isin⁡(15θ)
b
cos⁡(30θ)+isin⁡(30θ)
c
cos⁡(30θ)−isin⁡(30θ)
d
5cos⁡(6θ)−5isin⁡(6θ)
e
cos⁡(15θ)−isin⁡(15θ)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6=[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]−6.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)+isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−6 and φ=5θ. Substituting in these values, we get 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6=[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]−6=cos⁡(−30θ)+isin⁡(−30θ).

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have cos⁡(−30θ)+isin⁡(−30θ)=cos⁡(30θ)−isin⁡(30θ).
